definitions.note: names a character in the play rather than giving a synonym

parts.note: solemn and grave both mean serious in manner
a digger is an informal name for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A serious Australian actor turns up in a production of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: someone who appears in Hamlet, where a gravedigger jokes with the prince over Yorick's skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy has a comic scene of grave-making labourers in the churchyard, so this figure is one of its characters.

indicators.note: something incomplete lacks its end, so the final letter of the journey word is dropped

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on the road and declares the trip over.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an enemy is to defeat them and drive them away in disorder.

indicators.note: reassembly means putting parts together again in a new order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman who never turns up at the regimental reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone who has long served, especially a former member of the armed forces.

parts.note: Noah's Ark is the ancient vessel of the Bible

explanation.surface: Noah's vessel sailing on through day and night alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall brings darkness, so the dark is a common noun for the hours of night.

clue.text: Pictures here, right in ship's kitchen

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right within the word for the ship's kitchen

parts.note: a galley is the cooking area on a ship

explanation.surface: Paintings are hung, oddly enough, in the cookhouse aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An art gallery is a place where paintings are displayed, so pictures are found there.

clue.text: An ounce of salon powder scattered

definitions.note: the ounce is an old name for a large Asian mountain cat

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small measure of face powder spilt across the floor of a beauty salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An ounce' reads as a weight, but the ounce is also the name of a big cat of Central Asian mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is an old name for the pale, spotted big cat of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Fashion-bustle refit for painted ladies, perhaps

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Altering a bustle to dress up some made-up society women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painted ladies' suggests heavily made-up women, but the painted lady is a species of insect; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted lady is a common orange-and-black species of winged insect, one example of the type.

parts.note: a slip of paper on which a voter marks support for one candidate who is standing at an election, not a stumble by someone on their feet

explanation.surface: Someone upright loses their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark a printed sheet to choose one of the candidates standing for election.

clue.text: Drove one mad, being so dewy-eyed

parts.note: drove someone mad means sent them mad
I is the Roman numeral one
mental is an informal word for mad

explanation.surface: Someone is driven to distraction by another's tearful nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy-eyed describes someone easily moved to tears by emotion or nostalgia.

explanation.surface: A tale-teller who also makes things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning a yarn is telling a tale; a fabricator invents falsehoods, a teller of lies.

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the letter for one sits within the mesh word

parts.note: a net is a mesh of cords
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A delicate creature trapped in a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and dainty both describe something small, tidy and elegantly made.

explanation.surface: Stopping work for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause from work is a short respite; repose also refreshes body and mind.

clue.text: Majestic Norman, sweet in the garden

explanation.surface: A regal Norman lord admires the flowers in his garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the Norman king William the Conqueror; the second is the flower sweet william, where the word follows 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conqueror was a royal Norman duke; sweet william is a cottage-garden flower bearing that name after its first word.

parts.note: a fellow is a man
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A man introduced as an artist who is up to date and French.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French artist.

indicators.note: spread means scattered out, so the letters of the cheese dish are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Welsh rarebit spread on toast for the umpire's lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter settles disputes, just as an umpire or judge does.

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A trooper given to swearing curious curses.
explanation.walkthrough: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, a soldier of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of the musketeers in Dumas's novel, a fighting man of the French king's guard.

clue.text: Unpleasant name given to filthy dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pig's pen, a byword for a dirty home

explanation.surface: A rude label applied to a squalid house.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant both describe something disagreeable.

clue.text: Grub commonly found in wheat stores

indicators.note: found in signals that the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Insect larvae are often discovered in the grain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like an insect larva but is slang for food; 'commonly' marks the answer as informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a colloquial noun for food, as is grub.

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
a T-junction gives T

explanation.surface: A motorway map shows a ring road, a junction and a bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England; 'bypass' is a verb meaning skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to skip it or leave it out.

explanation.surface: Setting sail from a harbour in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A genoa is a large jib on a yacht; the city is a major seaport in Liguria.

clue.text: Small and ugly-looking, like international financier

explanation.surface: A dwarfish, unattractive banker.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss bankers were dubbed 'the gnomes of Zurich', so a financier is said to be gnome-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes are small, ugly folk of legend; Zurich bankers were nicknamed gnomes.

clue.text: Kind of spoon or stick put in beer

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the stick word goes within the beer word

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a post is a stick set upright in the ground

explanation.surface: Stirring a pint with a spoon or a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle spoon has a handle topped by a figure of one of Christ's twelve disciples.

clue.text: This rustic, around fifty, would be affable

indicators.note: this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs
the clue says the rustic with the fifty letter around it would make the affable word, so that letter comes out of it

parts.note: pleasant and affable both mean friendly
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A country fellow of about fifty would be good company.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put L (fifty) into the answer and you get PLEASANT, so take L out of PLEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm labourer of the countryside, a rustic.

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Nel's pig has trampled a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel, also called baldmoney, is a mountain herb of the carrot family.

indicators.note: sound here means the word as it is heard, not as written

parts.note: the clue's own word, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone regretted making an impolite noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it; the past tense means felt sorry about.

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the river's name surrounds the letter

parts.note: the Dee is a river of Scotland, Wales and England

explanation.surface: A river floods a valley in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A dene is a narrow wooded valley.

indicators.note: buried in means concealed inside, so the letters lie within the title

explanation.surface: Pirate gold lies buried on Stevenson's island.
explanation.definitionFit: Reis were old Portuguese and Brazilian monetary units, plural of real.

explanation.surface: Pupils shout a warning down an empty tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: At British public schools 'cave!' (Latin 'beware') warned that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave is a hollow in rock; cave, Latin for beware, was the public-school lookout's cry when a master approached.

explanation.surface: A box for keeping playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an eccentric, amusing person; a case is also a box or holder.

clue.text: Said of a home in which revised rent is ideal?

indicators.note: revised means reworked or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a house whose new rent seems perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Residential describes an area or property used for living in.

parts.note: an imperial is a small pointed beard below the lower lip, so one hidden behind such facial hair

explanation.surface: An emperor in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing whiskers has a hairy face, as an imperial beard gives.
